definition_en: a very hard clear precious stone, or a shape with four equal sides
core_image: 黑绒布上放着一颗石头，灯一照，四面都射出细光
scene: 珠宝店的柜台上铺着黑绒，一颗石头被灯照着，四面都在闪。The diamond on the ring caught the light.
sceneCN: 这里 diamond 指「钻石」（第 1 个义项：一种极硬而透明的宝石）；句意是戒指上那颗钻石接住了灯光。

collocations.zh: 未经琢磨的钻石；外粗内秀的人

senses.title: A hard clear gem
senses.definition: a very hard clear precious stone used in jewellery
senses.definitionCN: 一种极硬而透明的贵重宝石，用于首饰
senses.example: The diamond on the ring caught the light.
senses.exampleCN: 戒指上那颗钻石接住了灯光。
senses.why: The hardest thing in the room is also the one that breaks light into pieces.
senses.whyCN: 屋里最硬的东西，也最会把光拆成碎片。

senses.title: A four-sided shape
senses.definition: a shape with four equal straight sides and two pairs of equal angles
senses.definitionCN: 四边相等、两对角分别相等的一种图形
senses.example: The tiles were laid in a diamond pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 瓷砖被铺成菱形图案。
senses.why: A square tipped onto one corner looks like a cut gem.
senses.whyCN: 一个方框用角立起来，就像一颗切好的宝石。

senses.title: The card suit
senses.definition: one of the four suits in a pack of cards, marked with a red diamond
senses.definitionCN: 一副纸牌中四种花色之一，以红色菱形为标记
senses.example: He played the ace of diamonds and won the trick.
senses.exampleCN: 他打出方块 A，赢了这一墩。
senses.why: A gem can become a small red mark on a card.
senses.whyCN: 一颗宝石，能变成纸牌上的一个小红记号。

intro.en: Diamond comes from Greek adamas, the unconquerable, through Latin and Old French, and it has always named the hardest stone.
intro.cn: diamond 来自希腊语 adamas（不可征服的），经拉丁语与古法语进入英语，一直指最硬的石头。

items.en: Adamas meant unconquerable, built from a- and daman, to tame.
items.cn: adamas 意为不可征服，由 a-（不）与 daman（驯服）构成。

items.en: The stone was named for its refusal to be cut or worn down.
items.cn: 这种石头因不肯被切开、被磨损而得名。

items.en: Latin adamas shifted toward the form diamans.
items.cn: 拉丁语 adamas 渐渐变成 diamans 这一形式。

items.en: French diamant gave English its spelling and its jewellery sense.
items.cn: 法语 diamant 给了英语拼写，也给了首饰这层意思。

items.en: The shape and the card suit borrowed the same pointed figure.
items.cn: 菱形与纸牌方块借用了同一个带尖角的图形。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the diamond stem, while the meaning group names other precious stones.
note.cn: 形近组共用 diamond 这个词干，近义组则指其他几种贵重石头。

entries.definition: a snake with diamond markings
hard and bright like a diamond
decorated with small sparkling stones
a cut stone of high value
a precious stone set in metal
clear mineral with a regular shape
entries.definitionCN: 形状规则而透明的矿物

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a stone on black cloth and end with a red mark on a playing card.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从黑布上的一颗石头开始，落到纸牌上的一个红记号。

normal.en: The Greek name meant unconquerable, and the stone still refuses the knife.
normal.cn: 那个希腊名字意为不可征服，这颗石头至今也不肯让刀。

normal.en: Diamond is a shape as well as a stone: a square standing on one toe.
normal.cn: diamond 既是石头也是形状：一个踮着一只脚的方框。

normal.en: The card suit keeps the gem as a small red rhombus.
normal.cn: 纸牌花色把那颗宝石留成了一个小小的红菱形。

normal.en: Hard things also make the best windows for light.
normal.cn: 坚硬的东西，也最会给光开窗。

normal.en: A rough diamond is a person worth cutting.
normal.cn: 未经琢磨的钻石，说的是一个值得打磨的人。

abstract.en: Picture a stone with many flat faces.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗有许多平面的石头。

abstract.en: Picture a ring held up against a lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚戒指被举到灯前。

abstract.en: Picture four white bases in dry grass.
abstract.cn: 想象干草地上四个白色的垒包。

examples.en: The diamond on the ring caught the light.
examples.cn: 戒指上那颗钻石接住了灯光。

examples.en: The tiles were laid in a diamond pattern.
examples.cn: 瓷砖被铺成菱形图案。

examples.en: He played the ace of diamonds and won the trick.
examples.cn: 他打出方块 A，赢了这一墩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 diamond 记成「带个蒙的」：dia 是穿过，mond 像「芒」，光穿过石头射出光芒，那就是钻石。

root: 来自希腊语 adamas（不可征服），经拉丁语与古法语 diamant 进入英语。本义是坚硬到不肯被切割的宝石，后来也指被切成菱形的东西，并用于纸牌的方块花色与棒球场的内场。

sensesIntro.en: From the hardest stone, to the shape of a cut gem, to a small red mark on a card.
sensesIntro.cn: 从最硬的石头，到切好宝石的形状，再到纸牌上的一个小红记号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clear stone with many flat faces throwing light in all directions.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗有许多切面的透明石头，把光射向四面八方。

branches.en: The first sense is the stone itself and its value.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是石头本身以及它的价值。

branches.en: The second sense is the outline of the cut stone.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是切好的石头的外轮廓。

branches.en: The third sense is that outline reduced to a card symbol.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是那个轮廓缩小成纸牌符号。

branches.en: The gem and the rhombus share one pointed figure.
branches.cn: 宝石与菱形，共用同一个带尖的形状。

branches.en: A floor pattern and a card suit both repeat a small diamond.
branches.cn: 地面图案与纸牌花色，都在重复一个小菱形。

intro.en: Diamond has a small family built on hardness, brightness and the pointed shape.
intro.cn: diamond 有一小族词，建在坚硬、明亮与尖角形状上。

latinIntro.en: The Greek base means unconquerable, and the family keeps that sense of something that will not yield.
latinIntro.cn: 它的希腊词基意为不可征服，这一族词保留着「不肯屈服」的意思。

items.example: The diamond is flawless.
items.exampleCN: 这颗钻石毫无瑕疵。

items.exampleCN: 她在晚宴上戴着钻石。

items.example: The surface has a diamantine shine.
items.exampleCN: 这个表面有钻石般的光泽。

items.example: A diamondback crossed the path.
items.exampleCN: 一条菱背蛇穿过了小路。

items.example: The film is diamondoid.
items.exampleCN: 这层膜是类金刚石结构。

items.example: The watch was diamonded.
items.exampleCN: 这块表镶着钻石。

items.example: They found diamondiferous rock.
items.exampleCN: 他们发现了含钻石的岩石。

items.example: The seats were set diamondwise.
items.exampleCN: 座位按菱形排列。

definition_en: a book in which you write what happens to you each day
core_image: 床头一本带小锁的本子，页边已经磨毛
scene: 女孩把本子塞到枕头下，小钥匙还挂在细绳上。She wrote three lines in her diary before sleeping.
sceneCN: 这里 diary 指「日记本」（第 1 个义项：每天记事情的本子）；句意是她睡前在日记本上写了三行。

senses.title: A book of daily records
senses.definition: a book in which you write what happens to you each day
senses.definitionCN: 每天把发生在自己身上的事写进去的本子
senses.example: She wrote three lines in her diary before sleeping.
senses.exampleCN: 她睡前在日记本上写了三行。
senses.why: A day is too large to keep, so a page is cut from it.
senses.whyCN: 一整天太大拿不住，就从上面裁下一页。

senses.title: The record itself
senses.definition: the daily record kept in such a book
senses.definitionCN: 记在这种本子里的逐日记录
senses.example: His diary of the voyage was published later.
senses.exampleCN: 他这次航行的日记后来出版了。
senses.why: The book can outlive the days it describes.
senses.whyCN: 本子能比它记下的那些日子活得更久。

senses.title: An appointment book
senses.definition: a book used to note appointments and dates
senses.definitionCN: 用来记约会与日期的本子
senses.example: The meeting is in my diary for Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 会议记在我周五的日程簿上。
senses.why: The same page holds what happened and what will happen.
senses.whyCN: 同一页上，既装已经发生的事，也装将要发生的事。

intro.en: Diary comes from Latin diarium, a daily allowance or daily record, from dies, a day, and entered English in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: diary 来自拉丁语 diarium（每日的口粮或逐日记录），源词 dies 意为一天，十六世纪进入英语。

items.en: Dies meant a day, and diarium meant a daily portion.
items.cn: dies 指一天，diarium 指每日的一份。

items.en: Soldiers received a diarium, a daily allowance of money or food.
items.cn: 士兵领一份 diarium，即每日的钱或口粮。

items.en: The word also named a book that set down events day by day.
items.cn: 这个词也指逐日记下事情的册子。

items.en: English diary meant a daily record of a person's own life.
items.cn: 英语 diary 指一个人自己生活的逐日记录。

items.en: It now also means a book for appointments and dates.
items.cn: 如今它也指记约会与日期的本子。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ary ending, while the meaning group names other books of record.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -ary 这一结尾，近义组则指其他几种记录本。

entries.definition: a place where milk is kept or sold
entries.definitionCN: 存放或出售牛奶的地方

entries.definition: a round face with numbers or marks
a person who keeps a diary
a book of daily thoughts or events
entries.definitionCN: 记录每日想法或事情的本子

entries.definition: an official record of events
a small book for writing notes

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a locked book under a pillow and end with a date circled on a desk pad.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从枕头下带锁的本子开始，落到桌垫上被圈起来的日期。

normal.en: Diary and dairy differ by one swapped letter and one whole world.
normal.cn: diary 与 dairy 只差一个字母，却是两个世界。

normal.en: Dies is a day, so a diary is a stack of days in paper form.
normal.cn: dies 是一天，所以日记本就是一叠纸做的日子。

normal.en: A diary keeps what the mouth was afraid to say.
normal.cn: 日记收着嘴巴不敢说的话。

normal.en: The same book remembers the past and warns about Friday.
normal.cn: 同一个本子，既记住过去，也提醒周五。

normal.en: Three lines a night becomes a life in one shelf.
normal.cn: 每晚三行，最后能装成一整架人生。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny key on a red string.
abstract.cn: 想象一根红绳上挂着小钥匙。

abstract.en: Picture a page ruled with faint blue lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一页印着淡蓝横线的纸。

abstract.en: Picture one square circled twice in pencil.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小方框被铅笔圈了两遍。

examples.en: She wrote three lines in her diary before sleeping.
examples.cn: 她睡前在日记本上写了三行。

examples.en: His diary of the voyage was published later.

examples.en: The meeting is in my diary for Friday.
examples.cn: 会议记在我周五的日程簿上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 diary 记成「带日记」：di 是日，ary 是本子，逐日写下的本子就是日记本。

root: 来自拉丁语 diarium，源词 dies 意为一天。本义是每日配给的口粮或钱，也指逐日记事的册子。十六世纪进入英语后专指记录个人日常生活的本子，后来也用来指记约会与日期的日程簿。

sensesIntro.en: From a page cut out of one day, to the record that outlives it, to a date waiting in the future.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一天里裁下的一页，到比那些日子活得更久的记录，再到一个等着你的未来日期。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small locked book with worn edges beside a bed.
core.cn: 核心意象：床头一本带锁、边角磨毛的小本子。

branches.en: The first sense is the book that receives the day.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是接住这一天的本子。

branches.en: The second sense is the record after many days.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是许多天之后留下的记录。

branches.en: The third sense turns the same page toward the future.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把同一页转向未来。

branches.en: The book and its contents are one object seen at two times.
branches.cn: 本子与它的内容，是同一件东西在两个时刻的样子。

branches.en: A record of the past and a plan for Friday share one cover.
branches.cn: 过去的记录与周五的计划，共用一个封面。

intro.en: Diary has a small family built on days and on the habit of writing them down.
intro.cn: diary 有一小族词，建在「日子」与「把日子写下来」这个习惯上。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base dies means day, and the family keeps that daily beat.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 dies 意为一天，这一族词都保持着这种逐日的节奏。

items.example: The diary has a red cover.
items.exampleCN: 这本日记是红封面的。

items.example: Her diaries fill a shelf.
items.exampleCN: 她的日记摆满了一架。

items.meaning: a person who keeps a diary
items.example: The diarist wrote every night.
items.exampleCN: 这位记日记的人每晚都写。

items.example: She diarizes her travels.

items.meaning: in the style of a diary

items.exampleCN: 这部小说是日记体的。

items.example: The notes are diarial.
items.exampleCN: 这些笔记带有日记性质。

items.example: The dial shows the hour.
items.exampleCN: 表盘显示着钟点。

items.example: The dairy sells fresh milk.
items.exampleCN: 这家奶场卖新鲜牛奶。

definition_en: to stop living, or to lose life and vigour as a plant or machine does
core_image: 一盏油灯烧到最后，火苗抖了一下，屋里忽然安静下来
scene: 病房的窗开着，风把窗帘吹起又落下。The old dog died quietly beside the bed.
sceneCN: 这里 died 指「死去」（第 1 个义项：生命终止）；句意是那条老狗在床边安静地死去。

collocations.zh: 死于（多指疾病、饥饿等内因）
死于（多指外伤、事故等外因）

senses.title: Life comes to an end
senses.definition: to stop living, said of a person or an animal
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物的生命终止
senses.example: Her grandfather died at the age of ninety.
senses.exampleCN: 她的祖父九十岁那年去世。
senses.why: The body keeps its shape for a while, but nothing answers from inside.
senses.whyCN: 身体还会保持一阵形状，可里面再没有东西回应。

senses.title: A plant dries up
senses.definition: to lose all life and become dry, as a plant does
senses.definitionCN: 像草木那样失去生机、干枯下去
senses.example: The flowers died after the first hard frost.
senses.exampleCN: 第一场严霜过后，那些花都枯死了。
senses.why: What was green turns brown and no water brings it back.
senses.whyCN: 原本发绿的东西变成褐色，再浇水也回不来。

senses.title: To long for something
senses.definition: to want something so strongly that the feeling fills you
senses.definitionCN: 强烈地想要某物，几乎填满整个心思
senses.example: I am dying to hear how the story ends.
senses.exampleCN: 我太想知道这个故事怎么结尾了。
senses.why: The wish is so large that ordinary words feel too weak.
senses.whyCN: 那份想要太大，平常的说法都显得太轻。

intro.en: Die came from Old Norse deyja and pushed the native English verb aside after the Norse settlements.
intro.cn: die 来自古诺斯语 deyja，在诺斯人定居之后挤掉了英语原有的说法。

items.en: A root dau- tied dying to the state of being dead.
items.cn: 词根 dau- 把「将死」与「已死」连在一起。

items.en: Deyja meant to die, and Norse settlers carried it into English.
items.cn: deyja 意为死去，诺斯定居者把它带进英语。

items.en: Steorfan was the old verb for dying, and it survives as starve.
items.cn: steorfan 是古英语里「死」的说法，后来变成 starve。

items.en: Die replaced the native verb and became the everyday word.
items.cn: die 取代了本土动词，成了日常说法。

items.en: The verb widened to plants, engines and eager wishes.
items.cn: 这个词随后扩展到草木、机器以及急切的盼望。

note.en: The look-alike group sounds close but means something else, while the meaning group offers softer ways to say the same thing.
note.cn: 形近组读音相近却另有意思，近义组则提供更委婉的同义说法。

entries.definition: to change the colour of cloth or hair
small cubes marked with spots and used in games
extremely serious or terrible
to lose life, especially in a disaster
to come to the end of life or of a fixed period
a gentle way to say that someone has died
entries.definitionCN: 说某人去世的委婉说法

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from a lamp going out to the strange wish that borrows the word for dying.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一盏灯熄灭，走到那句借「死」来形容的渴望。

normal.en: Die and dye sound alike: one takes life, the other takes colour.
normal.cn: die 与 dye 同音：一个带走生命，一个改变颜色。

normal.en: Die out is what happens when the last speaker falls silent.
normal.cn: 最后一个说话的人沉默时，就是 die out。

normal.en: A battery dies quietly, without a funeral.
normal.cn: 电池悄悄就没电了，连葬礼都没有。

normal.en: Dead is the state, death is the event, die is the act.
normal.cn: dead 是状态，death 是事件，die 是动作。

normal.en: Dying to know simply means the waiting hurts.
normal.cn: dying to know 不过是说，这份等待叫人难受。

abstract.en: Picture a flame shrinking to a blue point.
abstract.cn: 想象火苗缩成一个蓝色的小点。

abstract.en: Picture a rose bending over a dry stem.
abstract.cn: 想象一朵玫瑰在干枯的茎上垂下头。

abstract.en: Picture a clock that simply stops between two ticks.
abstract.cn: 想象一座钟在两次滴答之间停住。

examples.en: Thousands of species die out every year.
examples.cn: 每年有成千上万个物种灭绝。

examples.en: The engine died at the worst moment.
examples.cn: 发动机在最糟的时刻熄火了。

examples.en: He died of a fever when he was thirty.
examples.cn: 他三十岁那年死于高烧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 die 记成「呆」：人一呆住不动了，气也就断了，正是死去。

root: 来自古诺斯语 deyja，与 dead 同出一支日耳曼词根。它进入英语后取代了古英语的 steorfan，成为表示「死」的常用动词，后来又从人和动物扩展到草木枯萎、机器停转，以及「渴望到极点」的说法。

sensesIntro.en: From a body that stops answering, to a plant that dries on the stem, to a wish strong enough to borrow death.
sensesIntro.cn: 从不再回应的身体，到茎上干去的草木，再到强到要借「死」来形容的愿望。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flame that shrinks and goes out, leaving the room silent.
core.cn: 核心意象：火苗越缩越小，最后熄灭，屋子一下安静。

chain: A HEART GIVES ITS LAST BEAT
A WISH BECOMES TOO LARGE FOR WORDS

branches.en: The first sense is the plain ending of a life.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是生命平直的结束。

branches.en: The second sense gives that ending to plants.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把这种结束交给草木。

branches.en: The third sense turns the word toward a burning wish.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把词锋转向一种灼人的愿望。

branches.en: A person and a plant both stop, but only one is mourned.
branches.cn: 人和草木都会停下，只是其中一个会被人哀悼。

branches.en: In both cases something is lost if nothing changes.
branches.cn: 两种情形里，若什么都不改变，就会有东西失去。

intro.en: Die has a small family of words about ending, and about the dead.
intro.cn: die 带出一小族词，围绕终结，也围绕逝者。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base here; the family grows from a Germanic root shared by dead and death.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词根；这一族词出自与 dead、death 共有的日耳曼词根。

items.example: His death shocked the whole town.
items.exampleCN: 他的死震动了整个镇子。

items.example: The dead leaves covered the path.
items.exampleCN: 枯叶铺满了小路。

items.example: The snake carries a deadly poison.
items.exampleCN: 这种蛇带有致命的毒液。

items.example: They cared for the dying man all night.
items.exampleCN: 他们整夜照料那个垂死的人。

items.example: She kept an undying hope.
items.exampleCN: 她抱着一份不灭的希望。

items.meaning: as quiet or pale as death
items.example: A deathly silence filled the hall.
items.exampleCN: 大厅里一片死寂。

items.meaning: to make a sound or feeling weaker
items.example: Thick curtains deaden the street noise.
items.exampleCN: 厚窗帘减弱了街上的噪声。

items.example: He asked for paper on his deathbed.
items.exampleCN: 他在临终的床上还要纸笔。

definition_zh: 饮食；日常食物；节食；规定饮食
definition_en: the kind of food that a person or animal usually eats, or a limited plan of eating
core_image: 餐盘里一小块鱼、一把青菜、半杯水，旁边压着一张写满格子的纸
scene: 营养师把餐盘推回桌子中间，用笔敲了敲那张表格。Her diet is mostly rice, fish and green vegetables.
sceneCN: 这里 diet 指「日常饮食」（第 1 个义项：平时吃的东西）；句意是她的饮食主要是米饭、鱼和青菜。

senses.title: What one usually eats
senses.definition: the food and drink that a person or an animal normally takes
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或动物平时吃下喝下的东西
senses.example: A diet rich in fruit protects the heart.
senses.exampleCN: 多吃水果的饮食对心脏有保护作用。
senses.why: It is not one meal but the habit behind a hundred meals.
senses.whyCN: 它不算一顿饭，而是上百顿饭背后的那个习惯。

senses.title: Eating less on purpose
senses.definition: a limited plan of eating, usually followed to lose weight
senses.definitionCN: 为减轻体重而有意控制的一份饮食安排
senses.example: She went on a strict diet before the wedding.
senses.exampleCN: 婚礼前她开始严格节食。
senses.why: A diet here is a rule set by the person against the person.
senses.whyCN: 这里的节食，是人给自己立下、又用来对付自己的规矩。

senses.title: A constant supply of the same thing
senses.definition: a long unbroken supply of something dull or unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 长时间不断涌来的一堆枯燥或难受的东西
senses.example: The audience was fed a diet of old songs and short jokes.
senses.exampleCN: 观众被迫听了一堆老歌和短笑话。
senses.why: The word lends the idea of feeding to things that are not food.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把「喂」的意思借给了并非食物的东西。

intro.en: Diet goes back to Greek diaita, a way of living, and reached English through Latin and French.
intro.cn: diet 可追到希腊语 diaita（生活方式），经拉丁语和法语进入英语。

items.en: Diaita meant a way of life, including food, exercise and sleep.
items.cn: diaita 指一种生活方式，包含饮食、运动与睡眠。

items.en: Latin diaeta kept the medical sense of a regulated life.
items.cn: 拉丁语 diaeta 保留了「有节制的生活」这层医学含义。

items.en: Diete arrived in French as the food a sick person should take.
items.cn: 法语 diete 指病人该吃的东西。

items.en: English diet first named a fixed allowance of food and drink.
items.cn: 英语 diet 最初指定量配给的饮食。

items.en: It split into the daily fare of anyone and a plan to lose weight.
items.cn: 它分成两层：人人日常的吃食，以及减肥的计划。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sound of diet, while the meaning group covers food supply, cooking and nutrition.
note.cn: 形近组与 diet 读音相近，近义组则覆盖食物供给、烹饪与营养。

entries.definition: a piece of music for two performers
relating to what a person eats
entries.definitionCN: 与一个人所吃的东西有关的

entries.definition: a person who limits food to lose weight
entries.definitionCN: 为减肥而控制饮食的人

entries.definition: the process of getting the food a body needs
entries.definitionCN: 身体获取所需食物的过程

entries.definition: the food provided, especially at a meal or in a place
entries.definitionCN: 尤指一餐或某地提供的食物

entries.definition: the style of cooking of a country or a chef
entries.definitionCN: 一国或一位厨师的烹饪风格

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a plate of ordinary food and end with the word stretched to cover songs and jokes.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一盘平常饭菜开始，最后落到被拉去形容歌曲与笑话的那个词。

normal.en: Die with a t: die is what a strict diet tries to avoid.
normal.cn: die 后面加个 t：严格节食最怕的就是 die。

normal.en: A diet is not a meal, it is the pattern behind many meals.
normal.cn: diet 不是一顿饭，而是很多顿饭背后的模式。

normal.en: Go on a diet means the plan starts today, not tomorrow.
normal.cn: go on a diet 意思是计划从今天起，不是明天。

normal.en: A balanced diet needs colour on the plate, not just weight on the scale.
normal.cn: 均衡饮食要盘里有颜色，不能只盯着秤上的数字。

normal.en: A diet of bad news is still a diet, though nothing is eaten.
normal.cn: 满耳朵坏消息也叫一种饮食，虽然什么也没吃。

abstract.en: Picture a plate divided into small coloured sections.
abstract.cn: 想象一个盘子被分成几块颜色不同的区域。

abstract.en: Picture a chart on the fridge door with squares to tick.
abstract.cn: 想象冰箱门上贴着一张画满格子的表。

abstract.en: Picture a scale that moves only when nobody watches.
abstract.cn: 想象一台只在没人看时才动的秤。

examples.en: Poor diet is a leading cause of heart disease.
examples.cn: 不良饮食是心脏病的主要原因之一。

examples.en: He has been dieting since the spring.
examples.cn: 他从春天起就一直在节食。

examples.en: The children were given a steady diet of cartoons.
examples.cn: 孩子们被连续灌了一堆卡通片。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 diet 记成「戴饿特」：戴着一份饿，特意少吃，就是节食。

root: 来自希腊语 diaita（生活方式），经拉丁语 diaeta 与古法语 diete 进入英语。本义是「有节制的生活」，尤其指病人该遵守的饮食安排；后来一方面泛指日常吃的东西，一方面专指为减轻体重而设的限制。

sensesIntro.en: From the food a body lives on, to a rule aimed at the waist, to a stream of non-food things forced down the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 从身体赖以活命的食物，到针对腰围立下的规矩，再到硬灌进脑子的一堆非食物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plate that is measured, not merely filled.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只被量过的盘子，而不只是被装满的盘子。

chain: THE SAME WORD FEEDS THE MIND

branches.en: The first sense is simply the pattern of daily food.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是日常食物的那个模式。

branches.en: The second sense adds a purpose: to become lighter.
branches.cn: 第二个义项添上目的：让自己变轻。

branches.en: The third sense feeds the mind instead of the body.
branches.cn: 第三个义项喂的是脑子，不是身体。

branches.en: The same plate serves health and vanity.
branches.cn: 同一只盘子，既为健康，也为体面。

branches.en: Both are about taking in less of something on purpose.
branches.cn: 两者都是有意少摄入某种东西。

intro.en: Diet builds a small family around eating, weighing and advising on food.
intro.cn: diet 围绕吃、称量与饮食建议，长出一小族词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Greek diaita through Latin diaeta, a way of living rather than a single meal.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是经拉丁语 diaeta 而来的希腊语 diaita，指生活方式而非一顿饭。

items.example: Her diet changed after the move.
items.exampleCN: 搬家之后她的饮食变了。

items.example: The doctor asked about his dietary habits.
items.exampleCN: 医生问了他的饮食习惯。

items.example: Most dieters give up within a month.
items.exampleCN: 大多数节食者一个月内就放弃了。

items.meaning: an expert in food and health
items.example: The dietitian wrote a simple weekly plan.
items.exampleCN: 营养师写了一份简单的周计划。

items.example: Constant dieting can harm the body.
items.exampleCN: 长期节食可能伤害身体。

items.example: She dieted for months before the race.
items.exampleCN: 比赛前她节食了好几个月。

items.example: Many diets promise more than they deliver.
items.exampleCN: 许多饮食方案承诺得多，兑现得少。

items.example: The shop sells dietetic sugar.
items.exampleCN: 这家店卖适合控糖人群的糖。

definition_en: to be unlike something else, or to hold a different opinion
core_image: 两条并排的路在远处分开，一条进林子，一条通向河边
scene: 两兄弟站在岔路口，一个指左，一个指右。Their opinions differ sharply on this question.
sceneCN: 这里 differ 指「意见不同」（第 2 个义项：看法不一致）；句意是在这个问题上他们的意见差别很大。

senses.title: To be unlike
senses.definition: to be unlike something else in one or more ways
senses.definitionCN: 在某一方面或几方面与别的东西不一样
senses.example: The two plans differ only in cost.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个方案只在成本上不同。
senses.why: Put two things side by side and a gap shows itself.
senses.whyCN: 把两样东西并排一放，缝隙自己就显出来了。

senses.title: To hold another opinion
senses.definition: to disagree with someone about what should be said or done
senses.definitionCN: 在说什么或做什么上与别人看法不一致
senses.example: Doctors differ about how much exercise is enough.
senses.exampleCN: 医生们对运动多少才算够看法不一。
senses.why: Two people can look at one fact and walk away with two stories.
senses.whyCN: 同一个人事实，两个人看完能带走两套说法。

intro.en: Differ comes from Latin differre, to carry apart, built from dis-, apart, and ferre, to carry.
intro.cn: differ 来自拉丁语 differre，本义是分开搬运，由 dis-（分开）与 ferre（搬、带）构成。

items.en: Ferre meant to carry or to bear a load.
items.cn: ferre 指搬运，也指承担一份重量。

items.en: Differre meant to carry things apart, and so to be unlike.
items.cn: differre 指把东西分开放，因而引申为不同。

items.en: The same verb also meant to put off until later.
items.cn: 同一个动词还表示把事情推到以后。

items.en: English differ took the sense of being unlike and of disagreeing.
items.cn: 英语 differ 承接了「相异」与「意见不合」两层意思。

items.en: The verb now anchors a whole family: difference, different, differentiate.
items.cn: 这个词如今撑起一整族词：difference、different、differentiate。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the diff- shape, while the meaning group covers varying, contrasting and deviating.
note.cn: 形近组共用 diff 这一形状，近义组则覆盖变化、对比与偏离。

entries.definition: to delay something to a later time
not the same as another thing
based on a difference between groups
to change or be different from one case to another
entries.definitionCN: 在个案之间变化或不同

entries.definition: to show a clear difference between two things
entries.definitionCN: 显出两物之间的明显差别

entries.definition: to move away from an expected path or rule
entries.definitionCN: 偏离预期的路线或规则

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with two roads splitting and end with two people reading one fact in two ways.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从两条路分开开始，最后落到两个人把一个事实读成两种。

normal.en: Dis- pulls apart, and ferre carries: differ is to carry apart.
normal.cn: dis- 往两边拉，ferre 是搬：differ 就是把东西搬开。

normal.en: Differ from names the other thing; differ in names the part.
normal.cn: differ from 接另一样东西，differ in 接具体方面。

normal.en: Two clocks differ by a minute and nobody notices for a year.
normal.cn: 两只钟差一分钟，一年都没人发现。

normal.en: To differ is not to fight, though a fight may follow.
normal.cn: differ 不等于争吵，虽然争吵可能跟着来。

normal.en: Different is the adjective, difference is the gap itself.
normal.cn: different 是形容词，difference 是那道缝本身。

abstract.en: Picture two roads leaving one field and never meeting again.
abstract.cn: 想象两条路从同一片田野出发，再没交汇。

abstract.en: Picture two rulers laid side by side, one a little longer.
abstract.cn: 想象两把尺子并排放着，其中一把略长。

abstract.en: Picture two hands pointing at opposite ends of a map.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手分别指着地图的两端。

examples.en: Their answers differ in almost every detail.
examples.cn: 他们的答案几乎每个细节都不同。

examples.en: Opinions differ on whether the plan will work.
examples.cn: 这个方案是否可行，意见并不一致。

examples.en: The twins differ only in the colour of their eyes.
examples.cn: 这对双胞胎只有眼睛的颜色不同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 differ 记成「地分」：地一分两边，人就各站一边，于是不同、也不合。

root: 来自拉丁语 differre，由 dis-（分开）与 ferre（搬、带）组成，本义是把东西分开搬运。因为分开之后彼此不再相同，就生出「相异」；又因为各人把话带向不同方向，就生出「意见不合」。同源的 defer 保留了「推后」的古义。

sensesIntro.en: From two things carrying apart, to two minds carrying one question in different directions.
sensesIntro.cn: 从两样东西被搬向两边，到两颗心把同一个问题带向不同方向。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two paths that leave the same point and never rejoin.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条路从同一点出发，再没有并回。

chain: TWO MINDS READ THE SAME FACT

branches.en: The first sense is about objects and the gap between them.
branches.cn: 第一个义项说的是东西本身以及它们之间的缝。

branches.en: The second sense moves the gap into people and their views.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把这道缝挪到人以及人的看法里。

branches.en: In both cases something is measured against something else.
branches.cn: 两种情形里，都是拿一样东西去比另一样。

branches.en: Disagreement needs no anger; it only needs two positions.
branches.cn: 分歧不必带火气，只要有两个位置就够了。

branches.en: A difference in facts often turns into a difference in judgment.
branches.cn: 事实上的差别，常常就变成判断上的差别。

intro.en: Differ anchors a large family built on the Latin stem fer-, to carry.
intro.cn: differ 撑起一大族词，词干 fer- 在拉丁语里是「搬、带」。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin ferre, to carry, with dis- meaning apart.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 ferre（搬、带），前缀 dis- 表示分开。

items.meaning: to carry apart, hence to be unlike
items.example: The two versions differ in tone.
items.exampleCN: 这两个版本语气不同。

items.example: The difference is small but real.
items.exampleCN: 差别不大，却确实存在。

items.example: Every child learns in a different way.
items.exampleCN: 每个孩子学习的方式都不同。

items.example: He treats his two sons differently.
items.exampleCN: 他对两个儿子的方式不一样。

items.example: A child cannot differentiate the two sounds.
items.exampleCN: 孩子分不清这两个音。

items.example: Cell differentiation takes many steps.
items.exampleCN: 细胞分化要经过许多步骤。

items.example: She was indifferent to the result.
items.exampleCN: 她对结果漠不关心。

items.example: His indifference hurt her more than anger.
items.exampleCN: 他的冷淡比发火更伤她。

definition_en: the way in which two people or things are not the same
core_image: 两只几乎一样的手套并排放在桌上，其中一只食指处磨破了一小块
scene: 店主把两只手套摊在柜台上，让顾客自己找不同。The difference between the two coats is only in the lining.
sceneCN: 这里 difference 指「差别」（第 1 个义项：不一样的地方）；句意是这两件外套的区别只在衬里。

senses.title: The gap between two things
senses.definition: the way in which two people or things are unlike each other
senses.definitionCN: 两个人或两样东西彼此不一样的地方
senses.example: The only difference is the size of the box.
senses.exampleCN: 唯一的差别是盒子的大小。
senses.why: Lay two things side by side and the eye finds the seam.
senses.whyCN: 把两样东西并排一放，眼睛就找到了那道缝。

senses.title: An effect that can be felt
senses.definition: the change that something brings to a situation or a life
senses.definitionCN: 某事物给局面或生活带来的改变
senses.example: One warm word can make a real difference.
senses.exampleCN: 一句暖心的话真能带来改变。
senses.why: Here the gap is not between objects but between before and after.
senses.whyCN: 这里的缝不在两样东西之间，而在之前与之后之间。

senses.title: A quarrel among people
senses.definition: a disagreement that keeps two sides apart
senses.definitionCN: 把双方隔开的那种不一致
senses.example: They settled their differences over dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在晚饭时解决了分歧。
senses.why: Two views pull apart until the people stand on different banks.
senses.whyCN: 两种看法越拉越开，人便站到了两岸。

intro.en: Difference comes from Latin differentia, built on differre, to carry apart, and entered English through French.
intro.cn: difference 来自拉丁语 differentia，词根是 differre（分开搬），经法语进入英语。

items.en: Ferre meant to carry, and dis- meant apart.
items.cn: ferre 指搬运，dis- 指分开。

items.en: Differentia named the quality that kept two things apart.
items.cn: differentia 指把两样东西区分开的那种性质。

items.en: Difference arrived as a word for a dispute as well as a gap.
items.cn: 法语 difference 既指缝隙，也指争执。

items.en: English kept both the physical gap and the quarrel.
items.cn: 英语同时保留了具体的差别与人和人的争吵。

items.en: The phrase make a difference grew into everyday praise for small acts.
items.cn: make a difference 逐渐成了对小事的日常褒奖。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the fer- ending, while the meaning group names gaps, marks and contrasts.
note.cn: 形近组共用 fer 结尾，近义组则分别指缝隙、标记与对照。

entries.definition: polite respect shown to another person
not the same as another thing
based on a difference between groups
a clear difference between similar things
entries.definitionCN: 相似事物之间的清楚区别

entries.definition: an empty space or amount between two things
entries.definitionCN: 两物之间的空隙或差额

entries.definition: a difference made clear by putting things together
entries.definitionCN: 把事物放在一起而显出的差别

normalIntro.en: These hooks go from a worn fingertip on a glove to one warm sentence that changes a day.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从手套上一处磨破的指尖，走到一句能改变一天的话。

normal.en: Differ is the verb, difference is the thing you can point at.
normal.cn: differ 是动作，difference 是你能指出来的那个东西。

normal.en: Tell the difference means the eye has already done the work.
normal.cn: tell the difference 意思是眼睛已经分完了。

normal.en: Make a difference is a gap turned into a gift.
normal.cn: make a difference 是把一道缝变成一份礼物。

normal.en: A small difference in the lining can double the price.
normal.cn: 衬里上一处小差别，能把价钱翻一倍。

normal.en: Settle differences means the two banks join again.
normal.cn: settle differences 是让两岸重新接上。

abstract.en: Picture two gloves with one small worn spot between them.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手套之间只有一处磨破的小点。

abstract.en: Picture a thin line drawn between two almost equal circles.
abstract.cn: 想象两个几乎一样的圆之间画着一条细线。

abstract.en: Picture a door that opens because someone pushed it once.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门被谁推了一下，就开了。

examples.en: There is a big difference between knowing and doing.
examples.cn: 知道与做到之间有很大差别。

examples.en: A few kind words made all the difference.
examples.cn: 几句好话起了一切作用。

examples.en: The differences between the two reports puzzled the judge.
examples.cn: 两份报告之间的差异让法官困惑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 difference 记成「地分冷死」：地一分，两边就冷，差别与分歧都出来了。

root: 来自拉丁语 differentia，词根 differre 由 dis-（分开）与 ferre（搬）组成，本义是分开搬运。分开之后彼此不再一样，于是有了「差别」；各人把话带向不同方向，于是有了「分歧」。

sensesIntro.en: From a gap you can point at, to a change you can feel, to a quarrel that keeps two people apart.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一道能指出的缝，到一种能感到的改变，再到把两人隔开的一场争执。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin seam between two things that look almost the same.
core.cn: 核心意象：两样几乎一样的东西之间，那道细细的缝。

branches.en: The first sense is the visible gap itself.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是那道看得见的缝。

branches.en: The second sense turns the gap into an effect.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把这道缝变成一种作用。

branches.en: The third sense puts the gap between people.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把缝挪到人与人之间。

branches.en: A difference in things can harden into a difference in people.
branches.cn: 事物上的差异会硬化成人之间的隔阂。

branches.en: Settling a quarrel is itself a change that matters.
branches.cn: 解决争执本身就是一种要紧的改变。

intro.en: Difference belongs to the fer- family, all of it about carrying and being carried apart.
intro.cn: difference 属于 fer 一族，全都围绕搬与被搬开。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin ferre, to carry, with dis- meaning apart.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 ferre（搬、带），前缀 dis- 表示分开。

items.example: The difference is easy to see.
items.exampleCN: 这个差别很容易看出来。

items.example: Their tastes differ a lot.
items.exampleCN: 他们的口味差别很大。

items.example: We took a different road home.
items.exampleCN: 我们走了另一条路回家。

items.example: The second question was answered differently.
items.exampleCN: 第二个问题的回答方式不同。

items.example: Can you differentiate the two voices?
items.exampleCN: 你能分清这两个声音吗？

items.example: Differentiation makes each cell special.
items.exampleCN: 分化让每个细胞各有其职。

items.example: The crowd seemed indifferent to the speech.
items.exampleCN: 人群对那场演讲似乎毫不在意。

items.example: Her indifference ended the friendship.
items.exampleCN: 她的冷淡终结了那段友谊。

definition_zh: 不同的；有差异的；各种各样的
definition_en: not the same as someone or something else, or made up of several separate kinds
core_image: 一排一模一样的白杯子，只有最右边那只的把手朝外
scene: 老师把五张画摊开，让学生指出哪一张不一样。Every student in the class comes from a different town.
sceneCN: 这里 different 指「不同的」（第 1 个义项：不是同一个）；句意是班里每个学生都来自不同的小镇。

pos.zh: 不同的；有差异的；各种各样的

senses.title: Not the same as another
senses.definition: not alike in some clear way
senses.definitionCN: 在某处明显不一样
senses.example: Her answer was different from mine.
senses.exampleCN: 她的答案和我的不同。
senses.why: One thing is set against another and the two do not line up.
senses.whyCN: 把一样东西对着另一样，两者对不上。

senses.title: Several separate kinds
senses.definition: used before a plural noun to mean various ones
senses.definitionCN: 用在复数名词前，表示各不相同的好几种
senses.example: The shop sells different kinds of tea.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店卖各种不同的茶。
senses.why: The word stops pointing at one gap and starts counting many.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不再指一道缝，而是开始点数许多个。

senses.title: Unusual in a noticeable way
senses.definition: rather strange or special compared with what is expected
senses.definitionCN: 与一般情形相比显得奇怪或特别
senses.example: There is something different about his voice today.
senses.exampleCN: 他今天的声音有点不一样。
senses.why: Being unlike the group becomes a mark on the person.
senses.whyCN: 与众人不同，就成了这个人身上的一处标记。

intro.en: Different comes from Latin differre, to carry apart, and reached English through French different.
intro.cn: different 来自拉丁语 differre（分开搬），经法语 different 进入英语。

items.en: Ferre meant to carry, and dis- pulled things apart.
items.cn: ferre 指搬运，dis- 把东西往两边拉开。

items.en: Differens described two things moving away from each other.
items.cn: differens 形容两样东西彼此分开。

items.en: Different kept the plain sense of not being alike.
items.cn: 法语 different 保留了「不一样」这层直白意思。

items.en: English used it for unlike things and for unlike people.
items.cn: 英语用它形容不同的物，也形容不同的人。

items.en: It also took on the loose sense of several or various.
items.cn: 它还生出了「好几种、各种各样」的宽松用法。

note.en: The look-alike group is easily confused in spelling, while the meaning group sharpens the idea of being unlike.
note.cn: 形近组在拼写上容易混淆，近义组则把「不一样」说得更精确。

entries.definition: showing no interest or concern
polite respect for another person
showing a difference between groups
clearly separate and easy to tell apart
made up of many unlike kinds
entries.definitionCN: 由许多不同种类组成的

entries.definition: different from another person or thing
entries.definitionCN: 与另一人或另一物不同的

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from one odd cup in a row to a voice that sounds unlike itself.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一排杯子里的那只异类，走到一个听起来不像自己的声音。

normal.en: Different from is the safe choice; different to is British and equally old.
normal.cn: different from 最稳妥，different to 是英式说法，同样古老。

normal.en: Different kinds turns the word into a counter of sorts.
normal.cn: different kinds 把这个词变成了数种类的量词。

normal.en: One cup turned the other way makes the whole shelf different.
normal.cn: 一只杯子转了方向，整排架子就不一样了。

normal.en: Differ is the act, difference is the gap, different is the label.
normal.cn: differ 是动作，difference 是缝，different 是贴上去的标签。

normal.en: Being different is only lonely when the row refuses to turn.
normal.cn: 只有当整排都不肯转身时，与众不同才显得孤单。

abstract.en: Picture one white cup with its handle facing the wrong way.
abstract.cn: 想象一只白杯的把手朝错了方向。

abstract.en: Picture two leaves from the same tree, one with a torn edge.
abstract.cn: 想象同一棵树上的两片叶子，其中一片边缘破了。

abstract.en: Picture a voice that almost matches a recording.
abstract.cn: 想象一个声音，几乎和录音一致。

examples.en: Life here is different from life in the city.
examples.cn: 这里的生活与城里的生活不同。

examples.en: The box holds six different colours.
examples.cn: 盒子里装着六种不同的颜色。

examples.en: He looked different after the long illness.
examples.cn: 久病之后，他看起来不一样了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 different 记成「地分认特」：地一分，两边人认出的特点就不一样。

root: 来自拉丁语 differre（分开搬）的现在分词 differens，经法语进入英语。分开之后彼此不再相合，便有了「不同的」；用于复数名词前，又引申为「各种各样的」；用于人，则带出「与众不同」的意味。

sensesIntro.en: From one thing set against another, to a row of many kinds, to a person who does not fit the row.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一样东西对着另一样，到一排好几种，再到一个不合这一排的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one object in a row that faces the other way.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排东西里，有一只朝向了另一边。

chain: A ROW STANDS IN ONE SHAPE
THE EYE MARKS THE ODD ONE
THE ODD ONE GETS A LABEL
MANY KINDS FILL THE SAME SHELF
A PERSON BECOMES THE ODD ONE

branches.en: The first sense is the plain comparison of two things.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是两样东西的平直比较。

branches.en: The second sense spreads the idea over many items.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把这层意思铺到许多物件上。

branches.en: The third sense applies the label to a person.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把这个标签用到了人身上。

branches.en: Both describe a set that does not repeat itself.
branches.cn: 两者都在说一个不重复自己的集合。

branches.en: Variety among things becomes strangeness in one person.
branches.cn: 物之间的多样，落到一个人身上就成了奇怪。

intro.en: Different sits in the middle of a family that runs from differ to differentiate.
intro.cn: different 站在一族词的中间，这一族从 differ 一直排到 differentiate。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin ferre, to carry, and the prefix dis- separates.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 ferre（搬、带），前缀 dis- 表示分离。

items.example: They come from different countries.
items.exampleCN: 他们来自不同的国家。

items.example: The two accounts differ in one detail.
items.exampleCN: 两份叙述在一个细节上不同。

items.example: The difference surprised everyone.
items.exampleCN: 这个差别让所有人都吃惊。

items.example: Each child behaves differently.
items.exampleCN: 每个孩子的表现都不一样。

items.meaning: to make or see a difference
items.example: Good teachers differentiate their tasks.
items.exampleCN: 好老师会给任务分层。

items.example: Differentiation begins in the early embryo.
items.exampleCN: 分化在早期胚胎里就开始了。

items.example: He remained indifferent to praise.
items.exampleCN: 他对赞美一直无动于衷。

items.example: Indifference can be louder than anger.
items.exampleCN: 冷淡有时比怒火更响。

definition_zh: 困难的；难对付的；难相处的
definition_en: hard to do, hard to deal with, or hard to please
core_image: 一段陡坡上散满碎石，走一步滑半步，鞋底抓不住地
scene: 山道越走越窄，脚下全是松动的石子。The last question was too difficult to answer in one minute.
sceneCN: 这里 difficult 指「困难的」（第 1 个义项：不容易做到）；句意是最后一道题太难，一分钟内答不出来。

pos.zh: 困难的；难对付的；难相处的

senses.title: Hard to do
senses.definition: needing much effort or skill to finish
senses.definitionCN: 需要花很多力气或本事才能完成
senses.example: Climbing the north face is difficult even for experts.
senses.exampleCN: 即使对行家来说，爬北壁也很难。
senses.why: The task does not refuse you; it only makes every step cost more.
senses.whyCN: 任务并不拒绝你，只是让每一步都更贵。

senses.title: Hard to handle
senses.definition: full of problems that are not easy to solve
senses.definitionCN: 充满不容易解决的麻烦
senses.example: The company is in a difficult position.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司处境艰难。
senses.why: The trouble is not in the work but in the ground under it.
senses.whyCN: 麻烦不在活儿本身，而在它脚下的地。

senses.title: Hard to please
senses.definition: not easy to satisfy or to get along with
senses.definitionCN: 不容易满足，也不容易相处
senses.example: He is a difficult man to work with.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个很难共事的人。
senses.why: The obstacle is now a person, and the person can answer back.
senses.whyCN: 障碍变成了一个人，而这个人还会回嘴。

intro.en: Difficult came back into English from difficulty, which descends from Latin difficultas, not easy.
intro.cn: difficult 是从 difficulty 反推回英语的，而 difficulty 出自拉丁语 difficultas，意为不容易。

items.en: Facilis meant easy, and dis- denied it.
items.cn: facilis 指容易，前缀 dis- 把它否定。

items.en: Difficultas named the state of being hard to do.
items.cn: difficultas 指事情难以完成的状态。

items.en: English took difficulty first, and difficult came later.
items.cn: 英语先收下 difficulty，difficult 来得更晚。

items.en: Difficult was formed again as an adjective from the noun.
items.cn: difficult 又由这个名词反推成形容词。

items.en: It stretched from tasks to situations and finally to people.
items.cn: 它从任务扩展到处境，最后用到了人身上。

note.en: The look-alike group is close in spelling, while the meaning group ranks several kinds of hardness.
note.cn: 形近组拼写接近，近义组则区分几种不同的「难」。

entries.definition: a problem that makes something hard
shy and unsure of oneself
too easy and not carefully thought out
needing great effort to do
asking for much time, skill or energy
entries.definitionCN: 要求大量时间、技术或精力的

entries.definition: hard to deal with and full of strain

normalIntro.en: These hooks start on a slope of loose stones and end with a man who argues with every plan.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一段碎石陡坡开始，最后落到一个对每个方案都要争一争的人。

normal.en: Dif- denies, facilis is easy: difficult is simply not easy.
normal.cn: dif- 是否定，facilis 是容易：difficult 就是不容易。

normal.en: The noun difficulty came first and the adjective followed it up the hill.
normal.cn: 先有名词 difficulty，形容词跟在后面爬上山。

normal.en: A difficult task costs time; a difficult person costs patience.
normal.cn: 难的任务费时间，难的人费耐心。

normal.en: Find it difficult is a polite way of saying it hurts.
normal.cn: find it difficult 是「这事让我难受」的客气说法。

normal.en: What is difficult today is only heavy, not impossible.
normal.cn: 今天的难，只是重，不是不可能。

abstract.en: Picture a boot slipping half a step on loose stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一只靴子在碎石上滑了半步。

abstract.en: Picture a knot pulled tighter by the hand that unties it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手越解，结反而越紧。

abstract.en: Picture a closed face that will not nod.
abstract.cn: 想象一张绷着的脸，怎么也不肯点头。

examples.en: It is difficult to learn a language alone.
examples.cn: 独自学一门语言很困难。

examples.en: She found the exam more difficult than expected.
examples.cn: 她觉得这场考试比预想的要难。

examples.en: The coach can be difficult when he loses.
examples.cn: 教练输了球时会很难相处。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 difficult 记成「地飞扣特」：地上飞石，扣子又特紧，处处都难。

root: 源自拉丁语 difficultas，由 dis-（否定）与 facilis（容易）构成，本义是「不容易」。英语先借入名词 difficulty，再由它反推出形容词 difficult。词义从「事情难做」，扩展到「处境难办」，最后用于形容「人难相处」。

sensesIntro.en: From a task that costs effort, to a situation that offers no clean way out, to a person who resists every plan.
sensesIntro.cn: 从费力的任务，到没有干净出路的处境，再到一个对什么方案都抵触的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a steep slope of loose stones where each step slips a little.
core.cn: 核心意象：一段满是碎石的陡坡，每一步都滑一点。

chain: THE GROUND OFFERS NO WAY OUT

branches.en: The first sense is about the effort a task demands.
branches.cn: 第一个义项说的是任务索取的力气。

branches.en: The second sense is about a situation with no easy exit.
branches.cn: 第二个义项说的是找不到轻松出口的处境。

branches.en: The third sense hands the hardness to a person.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把这份难交到一个人身上。

branches.en: Hard work and hard ground share the same cost.
branches.cn: 难做的活与难走的地，付出的是同一种代价。

branches.en: A difficult position is often made by difficult people.
branches.cn: 艰难的处境，往往是被难相处的人做出来的。

intro.en: Difficult brings a small family of words about effort, obstacles and the opposite of ease.
intro.cn: difficult 带出一小族词，围绕费力、障碍以及「容易」的反面。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin facilis, easy, and the prefix dis- denies it.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 facilis（容易），前缀 dis- 把它否定。

items.example: The road became difficult after the rain.
items.exampleCN: 下雨之后路变得难走。

items.example: He had difficulty breathing.
items.exampleCN: 他呼吸有困难。

items.example: She climbed difficultly up the last slope.
items.exampleCN: 她吃力地爬上最后一段坡。

items.example: The team met several difficulties at once.
items.exampleCN: 团队一下碰上好几处困难。

items.example: The answer was a facile one.
items.exampleCN: 那个答案过于轻巧。

items.example: A clear map facilitates the work.
items.exampleCN: 一张清楚的地图能让工作顺手。

items.meaning: ease in doing, or a place built for a purpose
items.example: The school has a new sports facility.
items.exampleCN: 学校有了新的运动设施。

items.example: He facilely dismissed the whole report.
items.exampleCN: 他轻率地把整份报告打发了。

definition_en: the state of being hard to do, or a problem that makes something hard
core_image: 一个人抱着一大摞箱子，最上面那只正一点点往一边滑
scene: 楼道很窄，他侧着身子往上挪，额角全是汗。She had difficulty finding the address in the dark.
sceneCN: 这里 difficulty 指「困难」（第 1 个义项：不容易做到的状态）；句意是她在黑暗里很难找到那个地址。

senses.title: The state of being hard
senses.definition: the fact of needing much effort or skill
senses.definitionCN: 需要花费很多力气或本事的情形
senses.example: He had difficulty breathing after the climb.
senses.exampleCN: 爬上去之后他呼吸困难。
senses.why: Nothing blocks the road; the road simply costs more than expected.
senses.whyCN: 路并没有被堵住，只是比预想的更费劲。

senses.title: A particular problem
senses.definition: one specific thing that stands in the way
senses.definitionCN: 挡在路上的某一具体麻烦
senses.example: The team ran into technical difficulties at once.
senses.exampleCN: 团队立刻碰上几处技术难题。
senses.why: The fog around the task hardens into a single object.
senses.whyCN: 任务周围的那团雾，凝成了一个具体的东西。

senses.title: A shortage of money
senses.definition: a period when money is not enough for what is needed
senses.definitionCN: 钱不够应付所需的一段时期
senses.example: The family fell into difficulty after the factory closed.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂关门后，这家人陷入拮据。
senses.why: Here the obstacle is not the task but the empty pocket.
senses.whyCN: 这里的障碍不是任务，而是空掉的口袋。

intro.en: Difficulty comes from Latin difficultas, in which dis- denies facilis, easy.
intro.cn: difficulty 来自拉丁语 difficultas，其中 dis- 否定了 facilis（容易）。

items.en: Facilis meant easy to do, from facere, to make.
items.cn: facilis 指容易做到，源自 facere（做）。

items.en: Difficultas named the quality of not being easy.
items.cn: difficultas 指「不容易」这种性质。

items.en: The word passed through French as difficulté.
items.cn: 这个词经法语 difficulté 传来。

items.en: English difficulty covered both effort and a specific obstacle.
items.cn: 英语 difficulty 同时指费劲与具体的障碍。

items.en: It also came to name a shortage of money.
items.cn: 它还进一步用来指缺钱。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the diffic- shape, while the meaning group names trouble, hardship and a blocking object.
note.cn: 形近组共用 diffic 这一形状，近义组则分别指麻烦、艰苦与挡路之物。

entries.definition: hard to do or to deal with
entries.definitionCN: 难以做到或难以应付的

entries.definition: shy and not confident
ease in doing something, or a built place
entries.definitionCN: 做事的便利，或建成的场所

entries.definition: problems that cause worry or effort
entries.definitionCN: 引起担忧或费力的麻烦

entries.definition: suffering caused by a lack of money or comfort
entries.definitionCN: 因缺钱或缺少舒适而受的苦

entries.definition: something that stands in the way of progress

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a heavy load slipping to a wallet that cannot cover the week.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一摞滑动的重箱子，走到一只撑不过一周的钱包。

normal.en: Difficult is the adjective, difficulty is the thing it names.
normal.cn: difficult 是形容词，difficulty 是它指的那个东西。

normal.en: Have difficulty doing means the hand hesitates before the work.
normal.cn: have difficulty doing 是说手在活儿前面先犹豫了。

normal.en: With difficulty means it was done, but nobody enjoyed it.
normal.cn: with difficulty 是说做成了，只是没人觉得轻松。

normal.en: One difficulty is a stone; many difficulties are a wall.
normal.cn: 一处困难是块石头，许多困难就是一堵墙。

normal.en: Money trouble borrows the same word as a hard task.
normal.cn: 缺钱的麻烦，借用了「难事」的同一个词。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of boxes leaning a little too far.
abstract.cn: 想象一摞箱子歪得有点过了头。

abstract.en: Picture a nail that bends with every blow.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚钉子，每敲一下都弯。

abstract.en: Picture an empty wallet on a table set for dinner.
abstract.cn: 想象摆好晚饭的桌上放着一只空钱包。

examples.en: She had great difficulty in reading small print.
examples.cn: 她读小字非常吃力。

examples.en: The project ran into difficulties last winter.
examples.cn: 这个项目去年冬天遇上了困难。

examples.en: He hid his financial difficulties from his family.
examples.cn: 他对家人隐瞒了自己的经济困难。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 difficulty 记成「地飞扣体」：地上飞石，扣子又扣得紧，身体处处受难。

root: 来自拉丁语 difficultas，由 dis-（否定）与 facilis（容易，源自 facere「做」）构成，本义是「不容易」。经法语 difficulté 进入英语，先指做事费劲的状态，再指具体的障碍，最后也用来指经济上的短缺。

sensesIntro.en: From the effort a task demands, to one hard obstacle, to a pocket that cannot last the month.
sensesIntro.cn: 从任务索取的力气，到一处具体的障碍，再到一只撑不过月的钱包。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a load that leans a little further with every step.
core.cn: 核心意象：一摞重物每走一步就再歪一点。

chain: THE WALL STANDS IN THE WAY

branches.en: The first sense is the general feeling of effort.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是那种整体的费劲感。

branches.en: The second sense turns that fog into one named obstacle.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把那团雾凝成一处有名字的障碍。

branches.en: The third sense moves the obstacle into the wallet.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把障碍挪进了钱包。

branches.en: Effort and obstacle are the inside and outside of one thing.
branches.cn: 费劲与障碍，是同一件事的里面和外面。

branches.en: A shortage of money is simply the hardest obstacle.
branches.cn: 缺钱不过是那堵最难翻的墙。

intro.en: Difficulty shares its base with difficult and with the fac- words about making and ease.
intro.cn: difficulty 与 difficult 同基，也与 fac 一族表示「做」和「容易」的词同源。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin facere, to make or to do, seen in facilis, easy.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 facere（做），在 facilis（容易）里也能看到。

items.example: The difficulty lies in the last step.
items.exampleCN: 困难就在最后一步。

items.example: The choice was a difficult one.
items.exampleCN: 这个选择很难。

items.example: He spoke difficultly after the accident.
items.exampleCN: 事故之后他说话很吃力。

items.example: The plan met difficulties early.
items.exampleCN: 计划一开始就遇上困难。

items.example: That is a facile explanation.
items.exampleCN: 那是个过于省事的解释。

items.example: Good light facilitates reading.
items.exampleCN: 光线好，读书就省力。

items.meaning: ease, or a place for an activity
items.example: The hotel has a small sports facility.
items.exampleCN: 这家旅馆有个小运动场所。

items.meaning: a power of mind or body, or a teaching body
items.example: The faculty met on Monday.
items.exampleCN: 全体教员周一开了会。

definition_en: to break and move earth, or to search deeply for something
core_image: 铁锹插进湿土，翻起一铲发黑的泥，旁边堆起小小的土丘
scene: 院子里那棵老树旁，男人一铲一铲往下探。They dug a narrow hole beside the fence.
sceneCN: 这里 dug 指「挖」（第 1 个义项：把土翻开）；句意是他们在篱笆旁挖了一个窄洞。

senses.title: To turn the earth
senses.definition: to break the ground and lift the soil away
senses.definitionCN: 把地面破开，把土铲走
senses.example: They dug a narrow hole beside the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在篱笆旁挖了一个窄洞。
senses.why: The hand works downward and the ground gives way.
senses.whyCN: 手往下使劲，地就让开了。

senses.title: To search deep below
senses.definition: to look for something by going far below the surface
senses.definitionCN: 钻到表层以下很远去找东西
senses.example: The team dug for old coins all summer.
senses.exampleCN: 整个夏天，这支队伍都在挖找古币。
senses.why: What is wanted lies under a layer, and the layer must be removed.
senses.whyCN: 想要的东西在一层东西下面，那层必须被搬开。

senses.title: A small cutting remark
senses.definition: a short remark that quietly makes fun of someone
senses.definitionCN: 一句不动声色取笑别人的短话
senses.example: He took the dig about his old car quietly.
senses.exampleCN: 别人挖苦他那辆旧车，他没作声。
senses.why: A remark can go under the skin the way a spade goes under soil.
senses.whyCN: 一句话能钻进皮肉，像铲子钻进泥土。

intro.en: Dig appears in Middle English as diggen, probably from an Anglo-French verb for cutting a ditch.
intro.cn: dig 在中古英语里写作 diggen，可能出自表示「开沟」的英法混合语动词。

items.en: Digue meant a dike, a bank raised to hold water.
items.cn: digue 指堤坝，为挡水而筑起的土埂。

items.en: Diguer meant to cut a ditch or a channel.
items.cn: diguer 指开沟、挖渠。

items.en: Diggen took the plain sense of moving earth with a tool.
items.cn: diggen 承接了「用工具翻土」这层直白意思。

items.en: The verb widened to hunting for buried things.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到寻找埋在地下的东西。

items.en: Dig also became a noun for a teasing remark and for a site being explored.
items.cn: dig 还变成名词，指一句取笑的话或一处发掘地。

note.en: The look-alike group is close in spelling, while the meaning group covers digging, tunnelling and searching deep.
note.cn: 形近组拼写接近，近义组则覆盖挖掘、打洞与深入寻找。

entries.definition: a person or machine that digs
a long wall of earth built to hold water back
the past form of dig
to remove earth carefully from a site
entries.definitionCN: 在现场小心地挖走泥土

entries.definition: to make a hole or tunnel and live in it
entries.definitionCN: 打洞或钻隧道并住在里面

entries.definition: to search deeply into a subject or a container
entries.definitionCN: 深入探究某个题目或翻找容器

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a spade biting wet soil and end with a remark that bites a person.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从铁锹咬进湿土开始，最后落到一句咬人的话。

normal.en: Dig, dug, dug: the vowel drops as the spade goes down.
normal.cn: dig、dug、dug：铲子往下走，元音也跟着沉下去。

normal.en: Dig up brings to the surface; dig into goes further in.
normal.cn: dig up 是把东西翻上来，dig into 是继续往里走。

normal.en: Dig deep is advice for muscles and for courage.
normal.cn: dig deep 既是对肌肉说的，也是对勇气说的。

normal.en: An archaeologist digs slowly because the past breaks easily.
normal.cn: 考古的人挖得慢，因为过去一碰就碎。

normal.en: A dig in conversation leaves no hole, only a bruise.
normal.cn: 话里的 dig 不留洞，只留一块淤青。

abstract.en: Picture a spade cutting a clean line in dark soil.
abstract.cn: 想象铁锹在黑土上切出一道干净的线。

abstract.en: Picture a small hill of earth growing beside a hole.
abstract.cn: 想象洞旁边慢慢堆起一座小土丘。

abstract.en: Picture a hand brushing dust off something buried.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手拂去埋着的东西上的土。

examples.en: The dog dug under the gate again.
examples.cn: 那条狗又在门底下刨洞了。

examples.en: She dug into the old records for hours.
examples.cn: 她在旧档案里翻找了好几个小时。

examples.en: He made a quiet dig about her lateness.
examples.cn: 他轻声挖苦了一句她迟到的事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dig 记成「地哥」：地哥拿着铲子，一寸寸往地里探。

root: 中古英语作 diggen，可能来自表示「开沟」的英法混合语 diguer，而 digue 指堤坝。本义是用工具翻土开沟，后来扩展到挖掘寻找埋藏之物，也用于比喻深入探究；作名词时，又指一句带刺的取笑话或一处发掘现场。

sensesIntro.en: From a spade lifting soil, to a search under the surface, to a remark that goes under the skin.
sensesIntro.cn: 从铁锹翻土，到地表之下的寻找，再到一句钻进皮肉的话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spade biting into wet soil and lifting it aside.
core.cn: 核心意象：铁锹咬进湿土，再把它掀到一边。

chain: A WORD CUTS UNDER THE SKIN

branches.en: The first sense is the plain act of moving earth.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是翻土这个直白动作。

branches.en: The second sense adds a purpose and a depth.
branches.cn: 第二个义项添上了目的与深度。

branches.en: The third sense turns the tool into a remark.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把工具换成了一句话。

branches.en: Every excavation begins with one shovel of soil.
branches.cn: 每一次发掘都从一铲土开始。

branches.en: Both go below the surface, one for facts and one for feeling.
branches.cn: 两者都往表层以下走，一个找事实，一个碰感受。

intro.en: Dig forms a small family of tools, actions and holes, with almost no Latin help.
intro.cn: dig 长出一小族词，涉及工具、动作与洞穴，几乎不靠拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic and French in origin; there is no Latin base behind this family.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根出自日耳曼语与法语，这一族词背后没有拉丁词基。

items.example: They dig a well every spring.
items.exampleCN: 他们每年春天挖一口井。

items.example: The digger cleared the whole bank.
items.exampleCN: 挖掘机清空了整道土坡。

items.example: Digging here is slow and careful.
items.exampleCN: 在这里挖掘要慢而细。

items.example: They dug the trench by hand.
items.exampleCN: 他们用手挖了那条沟。

items.example: He digs the garden every autumn.
items.exampleCN: 他每年秋天翻园子。

items.meaning: a hole in the ground used as shelter
items.example: The soldiers waited in a dugout.
items.exampleCN: 士兵们在地洞里等着。

items.example: The soil here is barely diggable.
items.exampleCN: 这里的土几乎挖不动。

items.meaning: earth removed, or a place being worked
items.example: The old diggings are now a park.
items.exampleCN: 那片旧采掘场如今是个公园。

definition_en: a measurement of length, width or height, or one part of a situation
core_image: 一只木箱被卷尺量过三次，长、宽、高各贴一张小纸条
scene: 木匠把卷尺拉开，沿箱子的三条边各量一次。The room's dimensions are printed on the plan.
sceneCN: 这里 dimensions 指「尺寸」（第 1 个义项：长宽高的大小）；句意是这个房间的尺寸印在图纸上。

senses.title: A measured size
senses.definition: a length, width or height that can be measured
senses.definitionCN: 可以量出来的长、宽或高
senses.example: Check the dimensions before you buy the table.
senses.exampleCN: 买桌子之前先看尺寸。
senses.why: A thing in space always asks to be measured in more than one way.
senses.whyCN: 空间里的东西，总要被不止一种方式量过。

senses.title: One direction in space
senses.definition: one of the directions in which space or a model extends
senses.definitionCN: 空间或模型伸展的某一个方向
senses.example: A line has only one dimension.
senses.exampleCN: 一条线只有一个维度。
senses.why: Counting the directions turns a shape into a number.
senses.whyCN: 把方向数出来，形状就变成了一个数。

senses.title: One side of a matter
senses.definition: one part of a situation that must be considered
senses.definitionCN: 一件事中必须被考虑到的一面
senses.example: The story has a moral dimension as well.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事还有道德层面。
senses.why: Problems have depth too, and each depth is called a dimension.
senses.whyCN: 问题也有厚度，每一层厚度都叫一个维度。

intro.en: Dimension comes from Latin dimensio, a measuring out, from metiri, to measure.
intro.cn: dimension 来自拉丁语 dimensio（量出），词根是 metiri（测量）。

items.en: Metiri meant to measure land or length.
items.cn: metiri 指丈量土地或长度。

items.en: Dimetiri meant to measure out in full.
items.cn: dimetiri 指完整地量出。

items.en: Dimensio named the result of that measuring.
items.cn: dimensio 指量过之后得到的结果。

items.en: English dimension meant size as measured.
items.cn: 英语 dimension 指量出来的大小。

items.en: Science added the sense of an axis, and common use added the sense of an aspect.
items.cn: 科学添上「坐标轴」的意思，日常用法又添上「方面」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the men- sound, while the meaning group covers size, aspect and extent.
note.cn: 形近组共用 men 这一段音，近义组则覆盖大小、方面与范围。

entries.definition: to become or make smaller
to speak or write about briefly
having a certain number of dimensions
how large or small something is
one part or feature of a situation
entries.definitionCN: 情况的一个部分或特征

entries.definition: the area or degree something reaches
entries.definitionCN: 某物达到的范围或程度

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from three tape marks on a box to a story with a moral side.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从箱子上三道卷尺痕，走到一个有道德层面的故事。

normal.en: Measure, measure, measure: dimension is the count of directions.
normal.cn: 量一次，再量一次：dimension 就是方向的个数。

normal.en: A box needs three numbers; a story needs several sides.
normal.cn: 箱子要三个数，故事要好几面。

normal.en: Add a dimension means one more direction to walk in.
normal.cn: add a dimension 就是多出一个可走的方向。

normal.en: The same word measures a room and a moral question.
normal.cn: 同一个词既量房间，也量道德问题。

normal.en: Metiri is measure, and metre hides inside it.
normal.cn: metiri 是测量，metre 就藏在里面。

abstract.en: Picture a tape measure bent along the edge of a box.
abstract.cn: 想象卷尺贴着箱子边缘拐弯。

abstract.en: Picture three chalk marks at right angles.
abstract.cn: 想象三道互相垂直的粉笔线。

abstract.en: Picture a flat drawing that suddenly gains depth.
abstract.cn: 想象一张平面图忽然有了厚度。

examples.en: The sofa fits the dimensions of the room.
examples.cn: 这张沙发与房间的尺寸相合。

examples.en: Time is often called the fourth dimension.
examples.cn: 时间常被称作第四维。

examples.en: Her letter added a personal dimension to the case.
examples.cn: 她的来信为这个案子添了个人层面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dimension 记成「地门神」：门口的地要量一量，量出长宽高，就是尺寸。

root: 来自拉丁语 dimensio，词根 metiri 意为测量，前缀 di- 表示分开、逐项。本义是逐项量出的结果，即长宽高等尺寸；数学与物理把它抽象为「维度」，日常语言又把它引申为事情的「方面」与「规模」。

sensesIntro.en: From a tape laid along a box, to an axis in space, to a side of a question that must be weighed.
sensesIntro.cn: 从贴着箱子的卷尺，到空间中的一根轴，再到一个问题必须被衡量的那一面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three tape marks at right angles on one wooden box.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只木箱上三道互相垂直的卷尺痕。

branches.en: The first sense is the measured size of a thing.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是东西被量出来的大小。

branches.en: The second sense is a direction in space.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是空间里的一个方向。

branches.en: The third sense is a side of a situation.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是事情的一个面。

branches.en: Measuring a box and naming an axis use the same idea.
branches.cn: 量一只箱子与命名一根轴，用的是同一个想法。

branches.en: Depth in space becomes depth in meaning.
branches.cn: 空间里的深度，变成了意思上的深度。

intro.en: Dimension joins a family of measuring words built on the Latin root metiri.
intro.cn: dimension 加入一族表示测量的词，词根是拉丁语 metiri。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin metiri, to measure, seen also in metre and measure.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 metiri（测量），metre 与 measure 里也能看到它。

items.example: The dimension of the box surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 这只箱子的尺寸让我们意外。

items.example: Write the dimensions on the label.
items.exampleCN: 把尺寸写在标签上。

items.example: The model is three dimensional.
items.exampleCN: 这个模型是三维的。

items.example: The two shapes are dimensionally equal.
items.exampleCN: 这两个形状在尺寸上相等。

items.example: Poverty is a multidimensional problem.
items.exampleCN: 贫困是个多层面的问题。

items.meaning: to find the size of something
items.example: Measure the wall before buying paint.
items.exampleCN: 买漆之前先量墙。

items.example: Each measurement must be exact.
items.exampleCN: 每项测量都必须精确。

items.example: The room is four metres wide.
items.exampleCN: 这个房间宽四米。

definition_en: the main meal of the day, usually eaten in the evening
core_image: 长桌上摆着冒热气的汤锅，几把椅子还空着等主人入座
scene: 厨房里汤锅咕嘟作响，孩子们被叫去洗手。Dinner was ready long before the guests arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 dinner 指「正餐」（第 1 个义项：一天的主餐）；句意是客人到之前很久，晚饭就做好了。

senses.title: The main meal
senses.definition: the largest and most formal meal of the day
senses.definitionCN: 一天中最丰盛、最正式的一餐
senses.example: We had dinner together every Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 我们每个周日一起吃正餐。
senses.why: The day has one meal that gathers people instead of just feeding them.
senses.whyCN: 一天里总有一顿饭，是把人聚起来而不只是填饱。

senses.title: A formal evening meal
senses.definition: an evening meal held for guests on a special occasion
senses.definitionCN: 为客人举办、带有场合意味的晚宴
senses.example: The hotel held a dinner for two hundred guests.
senses.exampleCN: 酒店为两百位客人办了晚宴。
senses.why: Food becomes the excuse for seating people in a certain order.
senses.whyCN: 饭菜成了借口，真正要做的是把人按次序排好。

senses.title: A meal sold ready to heat
senses.definition: a complete meal prepared and packed for quick heating
senses.definitionCN: 预先做好、包装起来、加热即食的一餐
senses.example: He ate a frozen dinner alone in front of the screen.
senses.exampleCN: 他一个人对着屏幕吃了份冷冻速食餐。
senses.why: The word keeps the ritual while giving up the table.
senses.whyCN: 这个词留下了仪式，却丢掉了那张桌子。

intro.en: Dinner comes from Old French disner, which first meant the morning meal that broke a night of fasting.
intro.cn: dinner 来自古法语 disner，最初指结束一夜禁食的那顿早饭。

items.en: Jejunus meant fasting, and dis- undid it.
items.cn: jejunus 指禁食，前缀 dis- 把它解除。

items.en: Disjejunare meant to break the fast.
items.cn: disjejunare 指开斋、结束禁食。

items.en: Disner named the meal that ended the night.
items.cn: disner 指结束一夜的那顿饭。

items.en: The meal moved later in the day as work hours changed.
items.cn: 随着作息变化，这顿饭在一天里越挪越晚。

items.en: Dinner settled as the main evening meal in most homes.
items.cn: 在多数家庭里，dinner 固定为晚上的主餐。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by a single letter, while the meaning group names meals of different weight.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个字母，近义组则区分分量不同的几顿饭。

entries.definition: a person eating, or a small cheap restaurant
entries.definitionCN: 用餐的人，或便宜的小餐馆

entries.definition: to eat a formal meal
a loud confusing noise
a light evening meal
a large formal meal for many guests
entries.definitionCN: 为众多客人办的正式大宴

entries.definition: food eaten at one time of the day
entries.definitionCN: 一天中某一时段吃的一餐

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a fast broken at dawn and end with a frozen tray eaten in front of a screen.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从天亮时结束禁食开始，最后落到对着屏幕吃掉的一只冷冻餐盒。

normal.en: Dinner once meant breakfast: the meal that broke the fast.
normal.cn: dinner 原本指早饭：那顿结束禁食的饭。

normal.en: Dine, diner, dinner: the verb, the person, the meal.
normal.cn: dine 是动词，diner 是人，dinner 是那顿饭。

normal.en: Dinner is a time as much as a dish.
normal.cn: dinner 既是菜，也是一个时刻。

normal.en: A dinner party is a meal with assigned seats.
normal.cn: 晚宴就是一餐配好了座次的饭。

normal.en: The word stayed warm even when the table disappeared.
normal.cn: 桌子没了，这个词还是暖的。

abstract.en: Picture a pot still steaming on a long table.
abstract.cn: 想象长桌上有一口还在冒热气的锅。

abstract.en: Picture empty chairs waiting for people to sit down.
abstract.cn: 想象几把空椅子等人坐下。

abstract.en: Picture one tray eaten under the light of a screen.
abstract.cn: 想象一只餐盘在屏幕的光下被吃掉。

examples.en: Dinner is at seven, so do not be late.
examples.cn: 晚饭七点开始，别迟到。

examples.en: She invited the whole team to dinner.
examples.cn: 她请整个团队吃晚饭。

examples.en: He cooked dinner while the rain beat on the window.
examples.cn: 雨打窗户时，他在做晚饭。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dinner 记成「定呢」：一家人定在桌边，饭才算正餐。

root: 来自古法语 disner，可追到拉丁语 disjejunare，由 dis-（解除）与 jejunus（禁食）构成，本义是「开斋」，即一天的第一顿饭。随着作息改变，这顿主餐逐渐挪到傍晚，于是 dinner 在多数地区固定为晚餐或正餐，并引申出宴会与速食餐的意思。

sensesIntro.en: From the meal that broke a fast, to a table set for guests, to a tray heated alone.
sensesIntro.cn: 从结束禁食的一顿，到为客人摆好的桌，再到一个人加热的餐盘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a steaming pot on a table with chairs waiting to be filled.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上的热锅，与等着被坐满的椅子。

branches.en: The first sense is the main meal itself.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是那顿主餐。

branches.en: The second sense adds guests and ceremony.
branches.cn: 第二个义项添上了客人，也添上了仪式。

branches.en: The third sense keeps the meal but loses the table.
branches.cn: 第三个义项留下了饭，丢掉了桌子。

branches.en: Any banquet begins as an ordinary dinner with more chairs.

senses.title: Without a turn
senses.definition: going from one point to another with nothing in between

senses.title: Saying it plainly

senses.title: To steer a group or a film

senses.why: Someone must hold the line so that others can follow it.

intro.en: Direct comes from Latin dirigere, to set straight, from dis- and regere, to rule or guide.
intro.cn: direct 来自拉丁语 dirigere（弄直），由 dis- 与 regere（引导、统治）构成。

items.en: Regere meant to guide a line or to rule people.
items.cn: regere 指把线拉直，也指治理人。

items.en: Dirigere meant to set something in a straight line.
items.cn: dirigere 指把东西摆成直线。

items.en: The participle directus described a straight path.
items.cn: 分词 directus 形容笔直的路。

items.en: English direct meant straight, and soon also to guide.
items.cn: 英语 direct 先指笔直，很快也指引导。

items.en: Film gave the verb its sense of steering a production.
items.cn: 电影让这个动词多出「执导一部作品」的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the rect- stem, while the meaning group covers straightness and guiding.

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with an arrow crossing a page and end with a director holding a whole play in line.

abstract.en: Picture a stage where every actor faces the same point.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台上所有演员都朝向同一点。

examples.en: The direct cause of the fire was a loose wire.
examples.cn: 这场火灾的直接原因是一根松动的电线。

examples.en: He directs a small company in the north.
examples.cn: 他在北方经营一家小公司。

examples.en: Please direct your questions to the manager.
examples.cn: 请把问题交给经理。

sensesIntro.en: From a line with no bend, to words with no padding, to a hand that keeps others on the line.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一条不弯的线，到一句不加铺垫的话，再到一只把别人按在线上手。

intro.en: Direct anchors the rect- family, all of it about straight lines and right guidance.
intro.cn: direct 撑起 rect 一族词，全都围绕直线与正确引导。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin regere, to guide straight, with the prefix dis- intensifying the setting.

items.exampleCN: 主任开了个短会。

items.example: The new directive takes effect Monday.
items.exampleCN: 新指令周一生效。

items.meaning: a list that points to names or files
items.example: Look it up in the phone directory.
items.exampleCN: 在电话簿里查一下。

items.example: The route was indirect but lovely.
items.exampleCN: 这条路绕，却很美。

items.example: They rectified the error at once.
items.exampleCN: 他们立刻纠正了错误。

definition_en: the line in which someone or something moves, points or develops
core_image: 一只指南针的针尖稳稳停住，四周刻着一圈细密的刻度
scene: 雾里看不清路，他低头看表盘上那根细针。The arrow points in the direction of the river.
sceneCN: 这里 direction 指「方向」（第 1 个义项：移动或指向的那条线）；句意是箭头指向河的方向。

senses.title: The line of movement
senses.definition: the line along which someone or something moves or points
senses.definitionCN: 人或物移动、指向所沿的那条线
senses.example: The bird flew in the direction of the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 那只鸟朝海的方向飞去。
senses.why: Every movement must choose one line and give up all the others.
senses.whyCN: 每一次移动都要挑一条线，同时放弃所有别的线。

senses.title: Instructions on how to do
senses.definition: words that tell someone how to reach a place or use a thing
senses.definitionCN: 告诉人怎么到某处或怎么用某物的那几句话
senses.example: Read the directions before you take the medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 吃药之前先看说明。
senses.why: A line on a map becomes a line of words.
senses.whyCN: 地图上的一条线，变成了一行字。

senses.title: The act of guiding
senses.definition: the control or leadership given to a piece of work
senses.definitionCN: 对一项工作给予的管理与带领
senses.example: The project grew under her direction.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目在她的指导下发展起来。
senses.why: The one who holds the line also decides where it will end.
senses.whyCN: 握住那条线的人，也决定它最后停在哪里。

intro.en: Direction comes from Latin directio, a setting straight, from dirigere, to guide.
intro.cn: direction 来自拉丁语 directio（摆正），词根是 dirigere（引导）。

items.en: Regere meant to keep a line straight or to rule.
items.cn: regere 指把线拉直，也指治理。

items.en: Dirigere meant to aim something along a line.
items.cn: dirigere 指让某物沿着一条线走。

items.en: Directio named the act of setting straight.
items.cn: directio 指摆正、对准这个动作。

items.en: English direction first meant the act of aiming.
items.cn: 英语 direction 最初指瞄准、对准的动作。

items.en: It widened to the line itself, to instructions and to leadership.
items.cn: 它扩展到那条线本身，也指说明与领导。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the direct- stem, while the meaning group names routes and bearings.
note.cn: 形近组共用 direct 词干，近义组则分别指路线与方位。

entries.definition: going straight without anything between

entries.definition: in a straight or immediate way

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a compass needle and end with a project led by one steady hand.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一根指南针开始，最后落到由一只稳手带起来的项目。

normal.en: Direction is direct turned into a thing you can point at.
normal.cn: direction 是 direct 变成能用手去指的东西。

normal.en: Ask for directions means asking for words in place of a map.
normal.cn: 问路，是用一句话代替一张地图。

normal.en: A sense of direction lives in the body, not in the phone.
normal.cn: 方向感住在身体里，不在手机里。

normal.en: In all directions means the choice has not been made yet.
normal.cn: in all directions 是说还没做出选择。

normal.en: Under her direction means she holds the line for everyone.
normal.cn: under her direction 是说她替所有人握着那条线。

abstract.en: Picture a needle settling after a long swing.
abstract.cn: 想象一根指针摆了很久之后停住。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow painted on a road at a turn.
abstract.cn: 想象拐角路面上画着一个箭头。

abstract.en: Picture a row of walkers all leaning one way.
abstract.cn: 想象一排走路的人都往同一侧倾。

examples.en: The wind changed direction in the afternoon.
examples.cn: 下午风改了方向。

examples.en: The package came with clear directions.
examples.cn: 包裹里附了清楚的说明。

examples.en: The research moved in a new direction.
examples.cn: 这项研究转向了一个新方向。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 direction 记成「地雷克神」：地上的雷要绕开，得先看清哪边是方向。

root: 来自拉丁语 directio，由 dirigere（引导、弄直）而来，而 dirigere 又由 dis- 与 regere（拉直、统治）构成。本义是「摆正、对准」这个动作，后来指移动所沿的那条线，再引申为告诉人怎么走的说明，以及对工作的领导。

sensesIntro.en: From a needle choosing one line, to words that replace a map, to a hand that keeps a whole project on course.
sensesIntro.cn: 从指针选定一条线，到代替地图的几句话，再到把整个项目按在路上的那只手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a compass needle stopping on one line among many.
core.cn: 核心意象：指南针在许多条线里停住了一条。

branches.en: The first sense is the chosen line in space.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是空间里被选中的那条线。

branches.en: The second sense is the same line told in words.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是把同一条线用话说出来。

branches.en: The third sense is the hand that keeps others on it.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是把别人按在这条线上的那只手。

branches.en: A map and its instructions describe one path.
branches.cn: 地图与说明描述的是同一条路。

branches.en: Good instructions are leadership written down.
branches.cn: 好的说明，就是写下来的领导。

intro.en: Direction sits at the centre of the rect- family of straight lines and guidance.
intro.cn: direction 位于 rect 一族的中心，这一族围绕直线与引导。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin regere, to guide straight, reached through dirigere.

items.meaning: a list that points to things

definition_en: in a straight or immediate way, with nothing in between
core_image: 一束光穿过敞开的窗，直直落在桌面，不碰墙也不拐弯
scene: 窗子正对着太阳，光一路照到桌中央。The road runs directly to the harbour.
sceneCN: 这里 directly 指「径直地」（第 1 个义项：不绕路）；句意是这条路直通港口。

senses.title: By a straight path
senses.definition: along a line with no turn and nothing in the way
senses.definitionCN: 沿着一条不拐弯、也没有遮挡的线
senses.example: The road runs directly to the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路直通港口。
senses.why: The shortest path is also the least eventful.
senses.whyCN: 最短的路线，也是最没有故事的一条。

senses.title: With no one in between
senses.definition: done by the person or thing itself, without another hand
senses.definitionCN: 由本人或本物完成，中间不经别人的手
senses.example: You can speak directly to the manager.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以直接和经理谈。
senses.why: A chain of hands slows every message and changes it.
senses.whyCN: 一串手递过去，消息既变慢也变形。

senses.title: At once, without delay
senses.definition: immediately after something happens
senses.definitionCN: 在事情发生后马上
senses.example: She left directly after the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 会议一结束她就走了。
senses.why: No turn in space becomes no gap in time.
senses.whyCN: 空间上不拐弯，就变成了时间上不留缝。

intro.en: Directly is direct plus the adverb ending -ly, built on Latin dirigere, to guide straight.
intro.cn: directly 是 direct 加副词词尾 -ly，词根是拉丁语 dirigere（拉直、引导）。

items.en: Regere meant to guide or to keep straight.
items.cn: regere 指引导，也指保持笔直。
